text: The paternal grandfather is a Duska whose mother was Maria Demko. Her birth record is believed to be in the Uzhhorod archives and has not been located.
The family comes from Senné and Iňačovce, Michalovce District.
The Duska line has been found in the 1869 Hungarian census and later records, and in a c. 1754 urbarial record where the household kept two beehives.
Kevin leans toward a Rusyn origin for the Demko side and is open to being wrong.

origin: Seen in a web search result
text: Kevin's own Duska one-name study site has an article on Senné house no. 73, headed by Jozef Duska, in the 1930 census. Only the search snippet was seen. The site itself has not been read and stays unread until the comparison phase.

text: A file named 'Anna Szlantai 1767', which the Sorter describes as a page from an online family tree naming several Duskas. The name and year are the owner's label. A Szalontai (Szlantai) is in the records here only as the wife of a János Nyemcsik of Senné in 1888 to 1903.

origin: The owner's words and file names, 12 Nov 2026.
text: A folder 'Duska Census' is beginning; its first part is named '1767 - Urbanarium'. File names assert an 'Andref Duska' and a 'Mihaly Duska' at Solymos, a 'Michael Demko' at Viszoka, a Kocsis at Csicser, Halas and Hornyák at Szenna, 'Knyerso' and Hudák at Solymos. The owner adds that his word files 'may be inaccurate'. A file named 'Guide to 1767 Urbarium', dated 15 February 2022 in its name, came with the images and was not opened.

The census files are named '1869 Census' and the compiled pages beside them '1868 Census ... Family Group Record'. Four 'family group record' files exist, one per sheet; they were not opened. A third party made a transcription and translation for the owner in January 2022.

origin: The owner's folder and file names, 12 Nov 2026.
text: A folder '1930 - BESA Whole Folder' holding one census sheet, named 'Besa - 1 - House of Igure Schwarz'. The owner kept a Schwarz household of Beša among his Duska census files. The mother of several Senné Duskas is an Erzsébet Schwarz.

File names in the 1930 census folders state the owner's conclusions: 'Stefan in house with Anna Nymcsik Mara Demko and Andrej Duska', 'Mihaily and Mikulas Ship Manifest', and notes such as 'see Anna Halasz' and 'see Beti Schwarz'. The first is borne out by the sheet. The owner collected Schwarz, Kocsis, Hresko, Knyezso and Demko households across eleven villages.

Five word files named '1930 [village] Initial List for [a transcriber]' for Iňačovce, Senné, Palín, 'Sarisske' and Vyšný Hrabovec: the owner drew up lists of census households for a hired transcriber. Not opened. Two of the villages, a 'Šarišské' place and Vyšný Hrabovec, are not otherwise in the archive.
